Control ambient light before tuning a robotic inspection camera

Windows, overhead fixtures and nearby work areas can change inspection images. The lighting environment needs attention before camera settings are finalised.

EVS Robot Blog ↗18 September 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1Videos 1

External light makes images inconsistent

EVST recommends checking windows, overhead lighting and adjacent work areas before adjusting an inspection camera. Light that changes during the day can make settings that work at one time unreliable at another.

Start with the real inspection cell

The accompanying video shows a part inside a cell with transparent panels and a window behind it, while a local light moves with the end device. This illustrates the layout but does not establish image quality or defect-detection accuracy.

Match light control to its source

The article discusses panels or enclosures, short light pulses and optical filters. Each measure should be linked to the source it addresses, including reflections from guarding and the workpiece itself.

Test under changing conditions

When a light or camera moves with the robot, shielding effectiveness can vary with position. Images need to be checked at times with different levels of interfering light before the inspection view can be treated as reliable.
